+# Issue #118 -- Context menus close ~350 ms after leaving a popover when sidebar is pinned
+
+## Class Diagram
+
+![Class diagram](118-tigerk9-class.png)
+
+## Sequence Diagram
+
+![Sequence diagram](118-tigerk9-sequence.png)
+
+## Q&A
+
+**Class diagram:**
+
+1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.
+
+   `SidebarProvider` and `contextMenuSlice`. `SidebarProvider` is mounted once near the top of `App` and owns the sidebar's show/hide state for the whole app. Every sidebar-related component reads that state through `useSidebar()`. Both the bug and the fix live in two of its effects: the `pointerover` listener and the effect that closes the context menu once the sidebar is hidden. `contextMenuSlice` is the single piece of Redux state behind _every_ right-click and "…" menu in the app. It explains how a sidebar timer could close a schedule's menu at all: `closeContextMenu()` isn't scoped to any particular menu, so whoever calls it closes whatever happens to be open.
+
+2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.
+
+   The dependency from `SidebarProvider` to `Popover`, labeled «observes [data-popover]». It doesn't show up in any `import`. The provider never references `Popover` in code. It detects it at runtime by checking whether the element under the pointer has a `data-popover` attribute, using a listener on the whole `document`. Because that check matches every popover in the app, the provider reacted to menus it never opened, which is the root cause. The fix makes this relationship conditional (it only exists while the sidebar is floating) instead of removing it, because a floating sidebar still needs it to stay open while its own budget-name menu is hovered. Combined with the «dispatch» `closeContextMenu()` dependency, it's what let a sidebar timer close an unrelated menu.
+
+3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?
+
+   The deeper problem is that the sidebar can't tell which menus it owns. Every menu goes through the same slice and the same `<ContextMenu>`, so the fix only removes the problem for pinned mode. A floating sidebar can still close a schedule's menu. I'd make ownership explicit, for example by recording whether the `contextmenu` event came from inside the sidebar (a `data-sidebar` attribute) and only tracking hover or closing menus while the sidebar owns the open one. I'd also pull the hover tracking out of `SidebarProvider` into a small hook such as `usePopoverHover(enabled)`, so the "only while floating" rule could be tested on its own instead of through the whole provider. That file is also still `@ts-strict-ignore`. This was a small issue, and doing much more would have taken it out of its original scope.
+
+**Sequence diagram:**
+
+1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?
+
+   It starts when the user (or the E2E test) clicks the "…" button on a schedule row while the sidebar is pinned, then moves the pointer onto the menu and back off it. On success, the menu stays open until the user picks an item. Clicking "Post transaction today" runs that item's action, then closes the menu the normal way through `ContextMenu.handleOpenChange(false)`, not because a sidebar timer fired.
+
+2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.
+
+   - **`ScheduleRow` fires `contextmenu`, which leads to `addItems(items)` (existing).** The "…" button doesn't call the menu directly. It dispatches a synthetic `contextmenu` event on the row, and `useContextMenu` turns that into a Redux update. That's why this menu shares global state with every other menu, including the sidebar's.
+   - **`document` sends `pointerover` to `SidebarProvider` (modified).** In the `[floating]` branch, `handlePointerOver` runs and starts the 350 ms hide timer. In the `[pinned]` branch this is now a lost message: the effect returns before adding the listener, so the event has no receiver and `hidden` never changes.
+   - **`SidebarProvider` calls `dispatch(closeContextMenu())` (existing call, modified condition).** This is the step that broke CI. It now also requires `floating`, as a backstop in case the sidebar is switched to pinned while a popover is hovered.
+
+3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?
+
+   - Closing the menu with Escape, or by clicking outside it. These use `ContextMenu`'s `pointerdown` listener and `Popover`'s `focusout` handling, which this change doesn't touch.
+   - Opening the menu with a right-click. After the event fires, it follows exactly the same path as the "…" button.
+   - The floating sidebar's own budget-name menu. It behaves as before and is covered by the existing unit tests.
+   - Switching from floating to pinned while a popover is hovered. That's a unit-test case, not a user flow.
+
+   One timing detail is also left out: the close effect keeps its `!hoveringPopover` check because React can run the close effect with the old `hidden = true` value before the layout effect's `setHidden(false)` has taken effect. I left these out to keep the diagram on the path that actually failed. Each one is either unaffected by the change or covered by `SidebarProvider.test.ts`.
+
+**Cross-cutting:**
+
+4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."
+
+   I used Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), in the same session that implemented the fix. It read the source files, then generated both diagrams as HTML/SVG and rendered them to PNG with Playwright. It also drafted these Q&A answers. Before drawing, it checked each element against the code: how `ScheduleRow`'s "…" button opens the menu (it dispatches a `contextmenu` event rather than calling anything directly), where `<ContextMenu>` is mounted (`FinancesApp`), the slice's fields and actions, and the E2E page model's `postNthSchedule` clicks. Corrections made along the way:
+   - **Layout fixes after reviewing each render:** overlapping labels, crossing connectors, and callouts too far from what they point at.
+   - **A clearer label:** `setContextMenuPosition({x, y})` was shortened to `setContextMenuPosition(pos)` to match the class diagram.
+   - **More accurate wording:** a callout that said "row 3" now says "the second schedule's menu", matching the issue, because the test's index is 0-based.
+
+   After the fix was implemented by AI, I manually checked the code change to make sure the bug was fixed as expected. I ran the app locally and checked the web implementation was fixed, and had Claude tell me what specifically I should test and what behavior to look for. As for the diagram itself, I looked over the entire thing after Claude generated it and it matched how the code works and in fact helped explain how everything worked more clearly to me.

diff --git a/upcoming-release-notes/fix-pinned-sidebar-closing-context-menus.md b/upcoming-release-notes/fix-pinned-sidebar-closing-context-menus.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..f72663c76

@@ -0,0 +1,6 @@
+---
+category: Bugfix
+authors: [tigerk9]
+---
+
+Fix menus closing on their own shortly after moving the mouse off them while the sidebar is pinned
// @ts-strict-ignore
import React, {
  createContext,
  useContext,
  useEffect,
  useLayoutEffect,
  useMemo,
  useRef,
  useState,
} from 'react';
import type { Dispatch, ReactNode, SetStateAction } from 'react';

import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';

import { closeContextMenu } from '#contextmenu/contextMenuSlice';
import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';
import { useDispatch } from '#redux';

const HOVER_HIDE_DELAY = 350;
const MENU_HOVER_OPEN_DELAY = 200;
export const SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS = 500;

type SidebarContextValue = {
  hidden: boolean;
  setHidden: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
  setHoveringSidebar: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>;
  onMenuButtonHoverStart: () => void;
  onMenuButtonHoverEnd: () => void;
  floating: boolean;
  alwaysFloats: boolean;
  reflows: boolean;
};

const SidebarContext = createContext<SidebarContextValue>(null);

type SidebarProviderProps = {
  children: ReactNode;
};

export function SidebarProvider({ children }: SidebarProviderProps) {
  const [floatingSidebar] = useGlobalPref('floatingSidebar');
  const [hidden, setHidden] = useState(true);
  const { width } = useResponsive();
  const alwaysFloats = width < 668;
  const floating = floatingSidebar || alwaysFloats;
  // When floating by choice (not forced by a narrow window), the open sidebar
  // takes up layout space so the main content shrinks instead of being covered.
  const reflows = !!floatingSidebar && !alwaysFloats;
  const dispatch = useDispatch();

  // A dropdown menu opened from the sidebar (e.g. BudgetName's) renders in a
  // portal, outside the sidebar's own DOM subtree, so hovering it never
  // triggers the sidebar's onMouseOver/onMouseLeave. Track hover of the
  // sidebar and of any open popover separately, then derive `hidden` from
  // both combined, so the sidebar (and its menu) stay visible while either
  // is being used, and only hide together once neither is hovered anymore.
  // This only applies while floating: a pinned sidebar is always visible, so
  // it ignores popovers and never closes context menus opened elsewhere.
  const [hoveringSidebar, setHoveringSidebar] = useState(false);
  const [hoveringPopover, setHoveringPopover] = useState(false);
  const [hoveringMenuButton, setHoveringMenuButton] = useState(false);

  // While the sidebar animates open or closed, the titlebar's menu button
  // slides with the main content and can end up under a resting cursor.
  // Ignore menu button hovers until the animation finishes so that can't
  // start an open/close loop.
  const isAnimatingRef = useRef(false);
  const isFirstRenderRef = useRef(true);
  const menuHoverTimeoutRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (isFirstRenderRef.current) {
      isFirstRenderRef.current = false;
      return;
    }
    isAnimatingRef.current = true;
    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
      isAnimatingRef.current = false;
    }, SIDEBAR_TRANSITION_MS);
    return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
  }, [hidden]);

  useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(menuHoverTimeoutRef.current), []);

  function onMenuButtonHoverStart() {
    if (isAnimatingRef.current) {
      return;
    }
    clearTimeout(menuHoverTimeoutRef.current);
    // Only open once the cursor rests on the button, so a mouse passing over
    // it on the way somewhere else doesn't open the sidebar.
    menuHoverTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
      if (!isAnimatingRef.current) {
        setHoveringMenuButton(true);
      }
    }, MENU_HOVER_OPEN_DELAY);
  }

  function onMenuButtonHoverEnd() {
    clearTimeout(menuHoverTimeoutRef.current);
    setHoveringMenuButton(false);
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!floating) {
      setHoveringPopover(false);
      return;
    }
    function handlePointerOver(e: PointerEvent) {
      const target = e.target as Element | null;
      setHoveringPopover(!!target?.closest?.('[data-popover]'));
    }
    document.addEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('pointerover', handlePointerOver);
  }, [floating]);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    if (hoveringSidebar || hoveringPopover || hoveringMenuButton) {
      setHidden(false);
      return;
    }
    const timeout = setTimeout(() => setHidden(true), HOVER_HIDE_DELAY);
    return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
  }, [hoveringSidebar, hoveringPopover, hoveringMenuButton]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (floating && hidden && !hoveringPopover) {
      dispatch(closeContextMenu());
    }
  }, [floating, hidden, hoveringPopover, dispatch]);

  return (
    <SidebarContext.Provider
      value={{
        hidden,
        setHidden,
        setHoveringSidebar,
        onMenuButtonHoverStart,
        onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
        floating,
        alwaysFloats,
        reflows,
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </SidebarContext.Provider>
  );
}

export function useSidebar() {
  const {
    hidden,
    setHidden,
    setHoveringSidebar,
    onMenuButtonHoverStart,
    onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
    floating,
    alwaysFloats,
    reflows,
  } = useContext(SidebarContext);

  return useMemo(
    () => ({
      hidden,
      setHidden,
      setHoveringSidebar,
      onMenuButtonHoverStart,
      onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
      floating,
      alwaysFloats,
      reflows,
    }),
    [
      hidden,
      setHidden,
      setHoveringSidebar,
      onMenuButtonHoverStart,
      onMenuButtonHoverEnd,
      floating,
      alwaysFloats,
      reflows,
    ],
  );
}

{"body":"## User Story\nAs a user with the sidebar pinned, I want a context menu (like a schedule row's \"…\" menu) to stay open until I\npick an item or click elsewhere, so that menus don't vanish while I'm using them.\n\nAs a developer, I want the \"Functional (shard 3/3)\" E2E job to pass reliably, so that PRs aren't blocked by a\nfailure unrelated to their changes.\n\n## Rough Scope: Small (2)\n- The root cause is a bug in my floating-sidebar change (9cc4a1f42) and is already identified (see Additional\n  Information). The fix is a one-condition change in `SidebarProvider.tsx`: only close context menus when the\n  sidebar is floating.\n- Test work is small: one existing unit test in `SidebarProvider.test.ts` assumes the non-floating case and\n  needs its setup changed, plus one new regression test.\n- Why not 1: the failure only reproduces on CI's slower runners, so confirming the fix takes one or more PR CI\n  runs rather than a quick local check.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] With the sidebar pinned, opening a context menu and moving the mouse into and back out of it does NOT close the menu.\n- [ ] With the sidebar floating, its own dropdown (e.g. the budget-name menu) still closes when the sidebar hides, as today.\n- [ ] `SidebarProvider.test.ts` has a regression test: pinned sidebar, hover a `[data-popover]`, move away, advance\n      350 ms, and `closeContextMenu` is NOT dispatched.\n- [ ] Existing `SidebarProvider` tests pass (updated where they assumed a pinned sidebar should close menus).\n- [ ] \"E2E Tests → Functional (shard 3/3)\" passes on the fix PR, including\n      `schedules.test.ts` › \"creates two new schedules, posts both transactions and later completes one\".\n- [ ] No changes to the E2E test itself; the app is fixed, not the test.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Floating mode: hovering an *unrelated* popover (e.g. a schedule row's menu) still slides the floating sidebar\n  open and can close that menu. Fixing that properly means having the sidebar track only the popovers it opened.\n  That's a bigger change, and I'll handle it in a follow-up.\n- The flaky \"Transactions › filters transactions › by payee / by category group\" E2E tests (seen in the same\n  shard). Investigate separately unless this fix happens to resolve them.\n- A reusable workflow for regenerating VRT screenshots in our fork.\n\n## Open Questions\n- Should a pinned sidebar track popover hover at all? Its `hidden` state has no visual effect when pinned, so\n  the `pointerover` listener could be skipped entirely in that mode instead of just gating the close effect.\n- For the follow-up: is tagging the sidebar's own popovers (e.g. a `data-sidebar-popover` attribute) the right\n  way to tell them apart from other popovers?\n- Do the flaky transaction filter tests share this root cause? (Filters use popovers, but not the context menu.)\n\n## Source\nLiam (@tigerk9) found this while getting CI green for PR #116 (VRT screenshot update). After the screenshots\nwere fixed, Functional E2E shard 3 kept failing on the same schedules test, even though #116 only changed PNGs\nand an AI log. The CI trace (from the `desktop-client-test-results-shard-3` artifact) pointed to\n`SidebarProvider`, which I changed in 9cc4a1f42 (\"Add floating sidebar auto resizing\").\n\n---\n\n## Observed Behavior (OB)\nWith the sidebar **pinned**, a context menu closes on its own about 350 ms after the mouse pointer leaves\n*any* popover. That includes a menu that opened just before the timer fired.\nIn CI, the schedules E2E test opens the second schedule's \"…\" menu just before this timer fires. The menu closes\nabout 35 ms after opening, and the test times out after 60 s waiting to click \"Post transaction today\".\n\n## Expected Behavior (EB)\nA context menu stays open until the user selects an item, clicks outside it, or presses Escape. Hovering or\nleaving other popovers should not close it while the sidebar is pinned.\n\n## Steps to Reproduce (S2R)\n**In CI (reliable on recent runs):**\n1. Open a PR that changes anything under `packages/` (so \"E2E Tests\" runs).\n2. Check \"Functional (shard 3/3)\": `schedules.test.ts:181` fails at line 218 (`postNthSchedule(3)`).\n\n**Manually (expected from the code; to confirm):**\n1. Open the demo budget with the sidebar pinned (the default).\n2. Go to Schedules and click the \"…\" button on any schedule row.\n3. Move the mouse onto the menu, then move it off the menu without clicking.\n4. Wait about half a second: the menu closes on its own.\n\n## Additional Information\n**Root cause:** `packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx`:\n1. A document-level `pointerover` listener sets `hoveringPopover` while the pointer is over any\n   `[data-popover]`, which sets `hidden = false`. This runs even when the sidebar is pinned.\n2. When the pointer leaves the popover, `hidden` returns to `true` after `HOVER_HIDE_DELAY` (350 ms).\n3. This effect then closes whatever context menu is open. I didn't check `floating` here:\n   ```ts\n   useEffect(() => {\n     if (hidden && !hoveringPopover) {\n       dispatch(closeContextMenu());\n     }\n   }, [hidden, hoveringPopover, dispatch]);","comments":[],"title":"[bug] Context menus close ~350 ms after leaving a popover when sidebar is pinned (breaks schedules E2E test)"}

It also settles the issue's first open question: when the sidebar is pinned, the `pointerover` listener isn't added at all, and `hoveringPopover` is reset to `false` ([SidebarProvider.tsx:104-115](packages/desktop-client/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProvider.tsx#L104-L115)). Floating mode works the same as before, so the budget-name menu still closes when the sidebar hides. **Not yet verified:** the "Functional (shard 3/3) passes" criterion, because no PR has run CI yet. **Minor edge case:** `floating` is now a dependency of the close effect.
